name: SWE-QA-Pro
role: benchmark (dataset + official scorer + official baseline agent)
commit_note: Latest commit on main at audit time ("update LICENSE"). No release tags exist on this repo.
license_data: CC BY 4.0 (arXiv page) / MIT (HF dataset card) -- discrepancy noted, not resolved by this project
environment_strategy: no vendoring of the agent/judge package; vendored ONLY the small, self-contained judge_prompt.txt file (exact rubric text) with this manifest as provenance. Judge API call shape (model, reasoning effort, verbosity, response parsing) is a faithful port in src/ant/benchmarks/sweqa_pro.py, verified against the real judge.py source read at the pinned commit.
model_used_by_official_baseline_agent: configurable via eval/configs/models.yaml -- gpt-4.1 (gpt-4.1-2025-04-14) is one of the officially supported models
local_modifications: None to the judge prompt text (vendored verbatim, byte-identical to the fetched official file).

Judge API call is a faithful re-implementation of judge.py's _score_one (same model, same reasoning effort, same verbosity, same JSON parsing/validation) -- not literally importing their package, since that would require standing up their full LangGraph/LangChain dependency tree for a scoring-only use case.
3x-averaging is applied per the paper's own documented protocol (confirmed via direct fetch of the official repo, not assumed).
official_baseline_agent_status: VERIFIED LIVE this session (Track A Stage 3): 2/2 real dev-question smoke runs succeeded end-to-end (qibo 9c20dc43873e8470, Pillow ea4dc7cad46d18c5) via external_wrappers/sweqa_pro_native_agent.py -> a real, pinned isolated venv checkout, driving the OFFICIAL ToolCallingAgent unmodified through a small new driver script (_ant_driver.py, checkout root, not part of the official release -- calls ToolCallingAgent.query() directly instead of eval/scripts/run_agent.py's own benchmark-loading CLI). No bug found in eval/sweqapro/ itself; no source patch applied (unlike HiFiRepoQA). Both runs: status=success, stop_reason='Forced after max iterations (25)' (used the full 25-step budget rather than stopping early), tool usage broke down correctly across the 3 official tools (view_codebase/execute_readonly_command/semantic_search). Physical-LLM-call counting via a LangChain BaseCallbackHandler (on_chat_model_start) caught a real, small discrepancy: the official agent's own steps_completed field (25 on the Pillow question) undercounted the true physical call count (26) by one -- same class of gap ANT's own baselines had before CountingOpenAIProvider fixed it. Combined smoke cost: ~$0.086 (2 questions, gpt-4.1). Fairness policy followed: GPT-4.1 generation (officially supported model_id in models.yaml), no ANT WorkerCards/Need Graph/recovery injected, official tool design/control flow fully preserved, generation and judging kept separate (no judge call made in this pass).
